searchText: Since this is final, would like to get another set of eyes on it: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/3790 Can I get another editor eyes on this? Non-normative change to a final EIP. I think it is fine, but I would like a bit more due diligence for final changes. <https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/3790> Approved 🙂 I'd be curious to know the next status for EIP-2464 & EIP-2364. Can this be moved to "Last Call" or "Final"? I am fine moving along the process to start with "Review". Just want to be sure that <@!194432762315407360> comment/suggestion is responded before making any pull request. Thoughts? Anything is OK for me, really My recommendation is to move it to Review, wait like 24 hours, then move it to Last Call. Then you would still be "following the process" and I won't have to fight with anyone later who says "but Felix didn't have to go to Review!", but we can still blaze through this process quickly. I doubt anyone will say anything during Review or Last Call other than editorial feedback, since this is already in production. sounds good! Will require Peter approving both PRs, or adding Pooja as an editor. 🙂 I have created a Pull Request to change the status. Will wait for <@!206016661470314496> approval. https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/3791 <@!301186049323958275> spent the last bit reading over the ruby related stuff. Got a good grip on it, one suggestion I have would be to relocate all the jekyll related files (basically .html, _config.yml, gemfile, etc...) into their own dedicated folder for readability and just separation of concerns. That would also make it super easy for a bot to tag the relevant people if they need to review changes to the ruby related code. I can open a pr to clean that up if theres some rough consensus around that, its relatively trivial Fine with me. Maybe <@642887713246150666> has opinions. Fine with me too. I'll follow the lead 🙂 wicked! ill look into it this weekend What is broken with jekyll/ruby? I forget what triggered all of this, I think GitHub dependabot posted a security issue PR and no one knows how to evaluate it. It is easy: as long as rendering is intact, it is fine. In most cases Ruby just crashes if there's an issue. What I used to do is compare the generated `_site` folder. I don't know how to even render the site. It is in the readme 😅 I aint got no time to read the EIPs readme. 😛 Ok it seems it got removed and iy only lists the serve option (which builds and runs an http server), but building works the same way: `bundle exec jekyll build`
